title: Turning sovereign AI into a business: Mistral AI sets up its Asia-Pacific headquarters in Singapore
excerpt: Mistral AI, the French AI company known as “Europe’s OpenAI,” announced on November 20 that it is setting up its Asia-Pacific headquarters in Singapore. It plan
content_html:
Mistral AI, the French AI company known as “Europe’s OpenAI,” announced on November 20 that it is setting up its Asia-Pacific headquarters in Singapore. It plans to expand its regional workforce to more than 200 people by 2027, hiring talent in research, engineering, and robotics.

First came Phoenix, then the headquarters

The headquarters did not appear out of nowhere. In November 2025, Mistral signed a memorandum of understanding with HTX, Singapore’s Home Team Science and Technology Agency, and in April this year the partnership was upgraded to a master strategic cooperation agreement on innovation. Phoenix, developed through their collaboration, is HTX’s first fully sovereign AI model family. Phoenix-VL 1.5 Medium, launched in June, can already recognize languages commonly used locally and across the region, and has been added to Home Team systems. The Asia-Pacific headquarters will operate as an “expanded science center,” developing sovereign AI models in three main areas: the public sector, high-tech manufacturing, and robotics. Its self-developed 8B model Robostral Navigate can autonomously navigate complex environments using only a single RGB camera.

Open weights, plus a customization business

The term sovereign AI emphasizes that customers keep control of their data, intellectual property, and product development. Mistral’s approach is to offer open-weight frontier models, then use tools such as Forge to customize them based on enterprises’ own data, with support for on-premises, private cloud, or hosted deployment. Capital has kept pouring in: starting with a €105 million seed round that set a European record, last September ASML took an approximately 11% stake for €1.3 billion and became the largest shareholder, and after a €3 billion Series D this September, the company reached a valuation of €21 billion. With that money, Mistral is putting down roots in Singapore and aims to deepen this “sense of control” business across Asia-Pacific.
